newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tenaga compensation up to courts-minister.
newsitem.headline: Tenaga compensation up to courts-minister.

text.p: Malaysian consumers who want compensation from utility company Tenaga Nasional Bhd for a peninsula-wide blackout in August will have to bring their cases to the courts, The Star reported on Wednesday.

It quoted Energy, Telecommunications and Posts Minister Leo Moggie as saying the government has no power to order Tenaga to to compensate consumers for the 12-15 hour blackout on August 3. "It is up to the courts to decide if the blackout was caused by Tenaga's negligence. As such it is up to consumers to take legal action to get compensation," Moggie was quoted as saying in Parliament on Tuesday.

"Legally, the government cannot order compensation to be paid. Only the court can order such compensation if it finds Tenaga negligent. Despite this, the government will study the matter first before deciding," he said.
The Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers has estimated the blackout cost its members some 123 million ringgit ($49.2 million) in lost production. ($1 = 2.50 ringgit)
